result.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
result.summary: A language model can name a brand without classifying it correctly. This study measures these outcomes separately for 1,000 B2B SaaS brands across 333 product categories. On Gemma 4 12B, with no external retrieval, category prompts elicit 510 brands (51.0%). A separate five-candidate category probe ranks the reference label first for 787 brands, a distractor first for 194, and yields little separation for 19. Among the 981 separated rankings, the error rate is 19.8%. It falls to 3.5% for the 547 brands with a winner-to-runner-up log-probability margin above 0.6. These are within-cohort measurements, not calibrated confidence estimates. Exploratory regressions associate technical coverage with recall and an owned-properties composite with category accuracy, but the composites use different adjustment sets and do not establish causal effects. Across four Gemma generations, measured recall is 39.8%, 44.3%, 51.1% and 51.0%. A separate representation-based sentiment measure has little linear association with customer ratings (r=0.03, n=921). The findings support reporting recall and category accuracy separately. Failure to elicit a brand does not establish its absence from model parameters or training data.

AI.brief_summary: 该文对 1,000 个 B2B SaaS 品牌做审计，在 Gemma 系列模型上将「能否唤出品牌名」与「五候选类别排序是否正确」分开测量，并用 log-prob margin 分区间报告错误率及探索性回归。
AI.relevance_reason: 把「能否唤起」与「是否正确归类」解耦、并以 log-prob margin 划分可靠性，可能为 LVR 中区分 latent 内容是否存在与其是否被正确使用、以及置信度驱动的证据筛选提供测量类比，可作核查线索。
